gap: No result ChatGPT got sets today's US prices beside the conditions behind each power rating: the Denon PMA-600NE costs $599 on denon.com, is rated 45 W/ch into 8 Ω across 20 Hz–20 kHz, and reaches its advertised 70 W only into 4 Ω at 1 kHz and 0.7% THD; the Yamaha A-S301 costs $429.95 at World Wide Stereo and is listed at 60 W x 2 (20 Hz–20 kHz), so the Denon costs $169.05 more for 15 W/ch less full-range power, and what the extra money buys is Bluetooth.
standout_why: I compared against recordplayeradvice.com (Denon vs Yamaha), stylusandsound.com best-stereo-amplifiers and best-integrated-amplifiers-under-1000, and puritybymonster.com. Recordplayeradvice gives both 8 Ω ratings but no prices, and says the two amps are in 'the same price bracket'. Stylusandsound shows no USD prices on either page and quotes the Denon only as '70 W per channel (4 ohms)'. Puritybymonster gives the Denon at $599, but only with the 70 W/4 Ω figure, and lists the WiiM Amp at $279, which is out of date because WiiM's store charges $329 today. Neither What Hi-Fi URL returned any content to compare against. None of these pages puts a current price next to the full-range 8 Ω rating, and none gives power or standby draw.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's choice of the Yamaha A-S301 as the default traditional amp. It is the cheapest of the four cards and has the most full-range 8 Ω power. Pay $169.05 more for the PMA-600NE only if you want Bluetooth. Among the streaming amps, the WiiM Amp at $329 and the Amp Pro at $399 are both rated 60 W/8 Ω, so the Pro's $70 extra buys features rather than power. The WiiM Vibelink Amp costs $299 for 100 W/8 Ω but has no streaming of its own. Our only listed amps are the Fosi BT30D Pro ($109.99) and the Crown XLS1002, and neither is a like-for-like answer for a home stereo integrated amp.
